item.title: [Episode 26] The Scent of Chanel Perfume and Gunpowder ([26화] 샤넬 향수와 화약 냄새)
item.description:
[Episode 26] The Scent of Chanel Perfume and Gunpowder ([26화] 샤넬 향수와 화약 냄새)

☞ View from Episode 1 (☞ 1화부터 보기)

☞ Character Introduction (☞ 등장인물 소개)

Philippines, Manila, Makati, 23rd floor of a newly built financial center: ‘GCI Networks’. (필리핀 마닐라 마카티 신축 금융 센터 23층 ‘GCI Networks’.)

Michelle Quo, CEO of GCI, was leaning against the floor-to-ceiling glass window, wearing a bright yellow silk dress that clung to her body, frantically scrolling through her smartphone. (GCI 대표 미셸 쿼는 몸에 딱 붙는 샛노란 실크 원피스를 입은 채 통유리 창가에 기대어 스마트폰을 정신없이 스크롤링하는 중이었다.)

“Clear all my remaining schedules. I feel like taking it easy today.” (“남은 스케쥴은 전부 비워줘요. 오늘은 좀 쉬고 싶네.”)

Tossing this one line to her secretary, Michelle was about to head home early. (미셸은 비서에게 이 한 마디를 던지곤, 집에 일찍 돌아갈 참이었다.)

Every time she hummed a tune and turned her head, her Van Cleef & Arpels Alhambra earrings swayed. On her right wrist was a Bulgari Serpenti bracelet densely studded with diamonds, while her left hand displayed a Cartier Panther watch and a Love bracelet, exuding a heavy presence. (그녀가 콧노래를 흥얼거리며 고개를 돌릴 때마다, 반클리프 알함브라 귀걸이가 찰랑거렸다. 오른손에는 다이아몬드가 촘촘히 박힌 불가리 세르펜티 팔찌를 감았고, 왼손에는 까르띠에 팬더 시계와 러브 팔찌가 묵직한 존재감을 드러냈다.)

The jewelry and designer clothes she wore were enough to buy a studio apartment in Seoul. (몸뚱아리에 걸친 보석과 명품 옷을 합치면 서울 오피스텔 한 채는 족히 살 수 있을 것 같았다.)

In the Southeast Asian defense market, the name ‘Michelle’ was known as a cheat key that could instantly bypass complex weapons acquisition procedures. Michelle could resolve in three months what would normally take three years through standard procedures, and customers who heard of this reputation came knocking at GCI’s door. Even without amateurishly embellishing a LinkedIn profile with flashy rhetoric, everyone in the industry knew the value of the name GCI. (동남아시아 방산 시장에서 ‘미셸’이라는 이름은 복잡한 무기 획득 절차를 단숨에 건너뛰게 만드는 치트키로 통했다. 미셸은 정상 절차로 3년이 걸릴 일을 3개월만에 해결해줬고, 그 소문을 들은 고객들은 알음알음 GCI의 문을 두드렸다. 굳이 아마추어처럼 링트인에 요란한 미사여구를 치렁치렁 달지 않아도, GCI라는 이름의 가치를 업계 모두가 알았다.)

For Michelle, these jewels were not just accessories. They were a dazzling armor that concealed her gray-zone identity as a ‘defense broker.’ (그런 미셸에게 보석들은 단순한 장신구가 아니었다. ‘방산 브로커’라는 회색 지대 신분을 가려주는 눈부신 갑옷이었다.)

“Should I postpone today’s meeting with Sentinel to next week?” (“오늘 센티넬쪽 미팅은 다음 주로 연기하면 될까요?”)

“Arrange it based on their schedule. I’m not in the mood for a meeting today.” (“그쪽 시간 봐서 알아서 맞춰봐요. 오늘은 미팅할 기분이 아니네.”)

“Since it’s not urgent, postponing it to next month seems fine.” (“급한 미팅이 아니니 다음 달로 미뤄도 괜찮을 듯합니다.”)

“Alright. See you tomorrow then.” (“그래요. 그럼 내일 봐요.”)

Just as Michelle was about to leave the office, an encrypted messaging app she rarely used rang out noisily. (미셸이 사무실을 나서려던 순간, 평소 쓰지 않던 암호 메시지 앱이 요란스럽게 울렸다.)

[Incoming Message: MSS Manila-bound package arriving today. Await retrieval.] ([수신 메시지: MSS 마닐라행 패키지 금일 도착 예정. 수령 요망.])

Upon checking the mysterious smartphone message, Michelle felt the knuckles on the back of her hand turn white. (미셸은 정체불명의 스마트폰 메시지를 확인하곤, 손등 뒤 뼈마디가 하얗게 불거지는 것을 느꼈다.)

Michelle slowly walked back into the office and looked out the window. (미셸은 다시 천천히 사무실 안으로 들어와 창밖을 바라봤다.)

The skyscrapers of Makati shimmered in the heat. The air between the building clusters, exceeding 40 degrees Celsius, clung to her skin like a sticky film, and the asphalt seemed ready to melt, visibly radiating heat. (마카티의 마천루들이 열기에 아물거렸다. 빌딩 숲 사이 공기는 섭씨 40도를 넘나들며 끈적한 막처럼 피부에 달라붙었고, 아스팔트는 금방이라도 흐물거릴 듯 열을 뿜어내는 것이 눈에 보일 정도였다.)

Whenever such messages arrived, Michelle was reminded again of the shaky foundation beneath the dazzling world she had painstakingly built. (이런 종류의 메시지가 올 때마다, 미셸은 자신이 힘겹게 쌓아 올린 화려한 세계의 바닥을 다시금 떠올렸다.)

A past like a pit hidden behind the jewels, a past she wanted to escape from at all costs. (보석으로 감싼 이면에 감춰진 구렁텅이 같은 과거, 어떻게든 빠져나오고 싶은 과거.)

But the option of refusal never existed in the first place. (하지만 거절이란 선택지는 애초에 존재하지 않았다.)

This is truly the last time (이번이 정말 마지막이다)

The bubbles from the carbonated water she had been drinking while humming stung the tip of her tongue. (콧노래를 부르며 마시던 탄산수의 기포가 혀끝을 쏘았다.)

Not long after, the office doorbell rang. (얼마 지나지 않아 사무실 초인종 소리가 울렸다.)

Ding-dong, ding-dong. (딩동, 딩동.)

Michelle approached with a relaxed demeanor and opened the door. (미셸은 여유로운 몸짓으로 다가가 문을 열었다.)

“Welcome to—” (“Welcome to—”)

Her greeting cut off the moment she opened the door. (문을 열자마자 인사가 끊겼다.)

The peaceful atmosphere of a summer afternoon changed in an instant. (여름 오후 안온한 일상의 분위기가 삽시간에 바뀌었다.)

A man, out of place in Makati’s refined setting, immediately killed Michelle’s bright smile. His rough gaze, as if he had just crawled out of a battlefield, and his sun-blackened skin were particularly striking. The faint smell of gunpowder and sweat instantly overpowered the Chanel perfume Michelle wore. (마카티의 세련된 풍경과는 어울리지 않는 한 사내가 미셸의 환한 웃음기를 단숨에 죽여버렸다. 전선에서 방금 기어 나온 듯한 거친 안광과 태양에 검게 그을린 피부가 특히나 눈에 띄었다. 묘하게 풍기는 화약 냄새와 땀 냄새가 미셸이 몸에 걸친 샤넬 향수를 단번에 짓눌렀다.)

“So… Are you Mr. Kim?” (“So… Are you Mr. Kim?”)

Michelle maintained a businesslike smile. (미셸은 비즈니스적 미소를 유지했다.)

Instead of answering, the man scanned the jewels around Michelle’s neck and wrists. It wasn’t the gaze of someone appraising the jewelry. It was the look of someone assessing the capability of the person he would be working with. (사내는 대답 대신 미셸의 목과 손목에 감긴 보석들을 훑었다. 보석 값을 매기는 눈이 아니었다. 자신과 함께 일할 자의 능력을 가늠하는 눈이었다.)

The man met Michelle’s eyes directly and asked back in broken English. (사내는 미셸의 눈을 정면으로 쏘아보며 어눌한 영어로 되물었다.)

“...You, Lily?” (“...You, Lily?”)

Michelle immediately felt her face stiffen. (미셸은 제 얼굴이 경직되는 걸 단번에 느꼈다.)

Lily. (릴리.)

That code name tightened around her neck, far heavier than the diamonds she wore. (그 코드네임은 그녀가 두른 다이아몬드보다 훨씬 무겁게 목을 조였다.)

“Nice to meet you for working together.” (“같이 일하게 돼서 반갑습니다.”)

Behind GCI’s flashy signboard, this man casually uttered the shackles she desperately wanted to escape but couldn’t. (GCI의 화려한 간판 뒤, 그녀가 어떻게든 벗어나고 싶었지만 벗어날 수 없는 족쇄를 이 사내는 아무렇지 않은 듯 읊었다.)

“……Come on in, Mr. Kim.” (“……안으로 들어오세요, 미스터 킴.")

Michelle opened the door wider a beat too late. (미셸은 한 박자 늦게 문을 열어 젖혔다.)

The man, who introduced himself as Kim Dong-seong, stepped inside without even nodding. (제 이름을 김동성이라 소개한 사내는 고개도 끄덕이지 않고 안으로 들어섰다.)

The smell of the battlefield spread through the office. (사무실 안에 전장의 냄새가 번졌다.)

Kim Dong-seong nonchalantly explained that North Korea’s Ministry of State Security had sent him here, and abruptly handed Michelle a bundle of documents. (김동성은 북한 국가보위성이 자신을 여기로 보냈다고 무심하게 설명하면서, 미셸에게 다짜고차 한 뭉치의 서류를 건넸다.)

[Grade-A Personnel Evaluation: Evan Yoon Dudaltech] ([갑급(甲級) 인물 평가서: 에반 윤 듀다엘테크])

Michelle quietly closed the door. (미셸이 조용히 문을 닫았다.)

“The higher-ups instructed me to deliver this to you.” (“상부에서 당신에게 이걸 전달해주라고 합니다.”)

“I got it. No need to rush. You Koreans are so impatient.” (“알았으니, 서두르지 마요. 조선인은 성격이 급하다니까”)

She tapped Kim Dong-seong’s shoulder and ushered him into the office. The tropical air, carrying the salty sea breeze of Manila Bay, was sliced by the cold air from the office air conditioner. (그녀가 김동성의 어깨를 톡치며 사무실 안으로 들였다. 마닐라 베이의 짭조름한 바닷바람을 머금은 열대 공기가, 사무실 에어컨이 뿜어내는 냉기에 잘려 나갔다.)

Click. (철컥.)

The sound of the door lock engaging echoed unusually loud. (도어락이 잠기는 소리가 유난히 크게 울렸다.)

🎧 Listen to the brilliant performances of AI voice actors in audio. (🎧 AI 성우들의 명연기를 음성으로 들어보세요.)

item.title: Song Young-gil: “Regret Nominating Jeong in Pyeongtaek? Like Saying I Should Have Aborted but Gave Birth” (송영길 “鄭 평택 공천 후회? 낙태해야 했는데 낳았다는 말”)
item.description:
Song Young-gil: “Regret Nominating Jeong in Pyeongtaek? Like Saying I Should Have Aborted but Gave Birth” (송영길 “鄭 평택 공천 후회? 낙태해야 했는데 낳았다는 말”)

Song Young-gil, a lawmaker running in the Democratic Party of Korea’s leadership election, took aim at his rival for party leadership, former lawmaker Jeong Cheong-rae, stating, “I think (Former Representative Jeong) has been consistently contemplating his own ‘independent politics’,” and added, “(Former Representative Jeong) became a lawmaker before me or President Lee Jae-myung, so perhaps he looks down on the president a bit.” (더불어민주당 당대표 선거에 출마한 송영길 의원이 당권 경쟁자인 정청래 전 대표를 겨냥해 “(정 전 대표가) 독자적인 ‘자기 정치’를 계속 고민해 왔다고 생각한다”며 “(정 전 대표가) 저나 이재명 대통령보다 먼저 국회의원이 됐으니까 뭔가 대통령을 약간 깔본다고 그럴까”라고 했다.)

In a radio interview on the 15th, Rep. Song said, “During the ‘Jeongtong’ (those connected with Jeong Dong-young) gatherings, (Former Representative Jeong) held a higher position than (President Lee),” and continued, “There should be respect for the head of state, not just for Lee Jae-myung as an individual, but isn’t there a lack of that respect?” Former Representative Jeong had worked alongside President Lee in the group ‘Jeongtong,’ which supported Jeong Dong-young—then the candidate of the Grand Unified Democratic New Party (the predecessor of the Democratic Party of Korea) in the 2007 presidential election and now the Minister of Unification. <<> Regarding Former Representative Jeong’s declaration that he would not run for president, Rep. Song said, “It could be interpreted as indirectly criticizing President Lee Jae-myung for becoming president after serving as party leader.” He added, “Who asked him to run for president? He still has four years of his term remaining, so it was baffling why he would bring that up.” <<> In response to Former Representative Jeong’s remark targeting him and former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok—stating that he had never left the party and had protected it—Rep. Song noted, “I think Former Representative Jeong can take pride in that,” but added, “I left the party to protect it without burdening it, not to abandon it.” <<> On Former Representative Jeong’s comment that his party should not have fielded a candidate in Pyeongtaek-eul, Rep. Song said, “It’s the same as telling your son, ‘I should have aborted you, but I gave birth to you’—isn’t that an incredibly irresponsible statement?” He added, “Former lawmaker Kim Yong-nam is currently the district chairperson for Pyeongtaek-eul; what happens to the party members who supported him?” (송 의원은 15일 라디오 인터뷰에서 “정통(정동영과 통하는 사람들) 모임을 할 때 (정 전 대표가 이 대통령보다) 더 높은 자리에 있었다”며 “자연인 이재명이 아닌 국가 원수에 대한 존중이 있어야 하는데 그에 대한 존중이 부족한 것이 아닌가”라고 했다. 정 전 대표는 2007년 대선 때 정동영 당시 대통합민주신당(더불어민주당의 전신) 후보(현 통일부 장관)를 지지하는 그룹 ‘정통’에서 이 대통령과 함께 활동했었다.)

item.title: Park Ji-won Also Shifts on 'Abolition of Supplementary Investigation Rights'... "Should Include Exceptions to Help the Vulnerable" (‘보완수사권 폐지’ 박지원도 선회… “약자 돕는 예외조항 둬야”)
item.description:
Park Ji-won, a five-term lawmaker of the Democratic Party of Korea, said on the 15th, "I also said I absolutely oppose the supplementary investigation rights, but I've revised that stance," adding, "For crimes against the socially vulnerable, including youth, women, and people with disabilities, it is right for the prosecution to have supplementary investigation rights." This marks a shift from the complete abolition of supplementary investigation rights to partial retention. <<> In an interview on YTN Radio's 'Jang Seong-cheol's News Myeongdang' that day, the lawmaker brought up the case of Jang Yun-gi in Gwangju, South Jeolla Province, while making this statement. As evidence of police downplaying and covering up crimes in the Jang Yun-gi case was uncovered through the prosecution's supplementary investigation, arguments within the ruling camp for retaining some supplementary investigation rights are gaining traction. <<> Park stated, "At yesterday's preliminary meeting of the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, I said, 'Our opinion isn't what matters; it's the public's thoughts that count. Especially since women's groups and Lawyers for a Democratic Society (Minbyun) oppose it, there's merit in that.'" He added, "Supplementary investigation rights should be applied within the scope of helping the vulnerable. We should include an exception clause." <<> He said, "The President also instructed us to deliberate thoroughly, and Minister of Justice Jeong Seong-ho has consistently suggested in the Legislation and Judiciary Committee that we should move in that direction," adding, "I said at the committee meeting that 'it's time for us to accept this.'" <<> Regarding the atmosphere within the party, Park predicted, "I believe things are heading toward (including an exception clause for supplementary investigation rights). There will be a lot of changes," noting, "Public opinion leans that way." (더불어민주당 5선 박지원 의원은 15일 “나도 보완수사권은 절대 반대한다고 얘기했는데, 수정했다”며 “사회적 약자, 청소년, 여성, 장애인 범죄 등에 대해선 (검찰이) 보완수사권을 갖는 것이 옳다”고 했다. 보완수사권 완전 폐지에서 일부 존치로 입장을 바꾼 것이다.)

item.title: U.S.-South Korea Coupang Dispute Leads to Unusual Temporary Return of Ambassador Kang Kyung-wha (韓美 쿠팡 이견에 강경화 주미 대사 이례적 일시 귀국)
item.description:
U.S.-South Korea Coupang Dispute Leads to Unusual Temporary Return of Ambassador Kang Kyung-wha (韓美 쿠팡 이견에 강경화 주미 대사 이례적 일시 귀국)

Kang Kyung-wha, South Korea's ambassador to the United States, will temporarily return to South Korea under the directive of Foreign Minister Cho Tae-yul. It is highly unusual for an ambassador to the U.S. to return not for a regular meeting of overseas mission heads but to coordinate pending issues, indicating that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs believes the disparity in perceptions between South Korea and the U.S. over the Coupang issue is seriously affecting overall bilateral relations. <<> Foreign Ministry spokesperson Park Il stated on the 14th, "Ambassador Kang will temporarily return from the 15th to the 19th under the foreign minister's directive to hold working-level consultations with relevant ministries on overall South Korea-U.S. relations." Ambassador Kang is expected to meet successively with officials from the National Security Office, as well as the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the Ministry of Science and ICT, and the Ministry of National Defense. <<> This move is analyzed as stemming from concerns that the ongoing Coupang issue is becoming a stumbling block in South Korea-U.S. relations, potentially disrupting the implementation of the comprehensive South Korea-U.S. Joint Fact Sheet agreed upon last year. On the 1st, the U.S. House Judiciary Committee released a report claiming Coupang faces hostile regulations in South Korea, and the following day, the White House stated, "Coupang has been targeted by the Lee Jae-myung government." <<> While the presidential office has stated that the contents of the U.S. House report "differ significantly from the facts," the South Korea-U.S. Joint Fact Sheet includes a pledge to "ensure that U.S. companies are not discriminated against or face unnecessary barriers." If the U.S. side perceives that Coupang is being discriminated against, it could hinder the implementation of other agreements, such as South Korea securing rights for uranium enrichment and spent nuclear fuel reprocessing, as well as the introduction of nuclear-powered submarines. South Korea and the U.S. have yet to set a schedule for follow-up consultations on implementing security agreements. This could also negatively impact the U.S. Trade Representative's ongoing Section 301 investigation into "overcapacity" and the imposition of tariffs on South Korea. <<> A diplomatic source stated, "There is a clear difference in the level of concern over the Coupang issue between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other ministries," adding, "I understand that Ambassador Kang will directly convey the seriousness she feels on the ground to the departments handling U.S. negotiations." Temporarily recalling an ambassador to the home country over diplomatic issues can sometimes carry a message of "protest" to the host country. However, when asked whether Ambassador Kang's return signifies a protest against the U.S., a Foreign Ministry official replied, "Not at all." (강경화 주미 한국 대사가 조현 외교부 장관의 지시에 따라 일시 귀국한다. 주미 대사가 정기 재외공관장 회의가 아니라 현안 조율을 위해 귀국하는 것은 상당히 이례적인 일로, 쿠팡 문제 등에 대한 한·미 간 인식 차가 양국 관계 전반에 심각한 영향을 주고 있다고 외교부가 판단한 것으로 볼 수 있다.)

item.title: Jeong Cheong-rae, After Holding Out, Accepts Preferential Voting… Pro-Moon Faction Says “A Calculated Move to Garner Sympathy Votes” (버티던 정청래, 선호투표 수용… 친명 “동정표 노리고 선회”)
item.description:
Jeong Cheong-rae, After Holding Out, Accepts Preferential Voting… Pro-Moon Faction Says “A Calculated Move to Garner Sympathy Votes” (버티던 정청래, 선호투표 수용… 친명 “동정표 노리고 선회”)

Jeong Cheong-rae, who had previously argued that preferential voting violates the party constitution and rules, stated, “I will accept it coolly.” Preferential voting, where candidates are ranked to prepare for situations where no candidate secures a majority, was widely seen as favoring former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok and lawmaker Song Young-gil. Within the pro-Moon Jae-in faction, some commented, “Jeong and his pro-Jeong faction’s swift acceptance, despite opposing preferential voting, seems like a calculation to appear as if they are yielding to unfavorable rules, thereby gaining sympathy votes from party members.” <<> On the 14th, the Democratic Party held a Supreme Council meeting and amended party rules, which previously only specified a 'runoff vote' for the party leadership election, to allow 'preferential voting or a runoff vote.' During this process, pro-Jeong Supreme Council member Lee Seong-yoon resigned his post, saying, “This is absolutely unacceptable,” but the outcome was that Jeong’s side, which had opposed the introduction of preferential voting, ultimately backed down. <<> Earlier, when the Democratic Party’s National Convention Preparation Committee decided on the 7th to introduce preferential voting, the pro-Jeong faction had protested for a week, claiming it “violates the party constitution and rules.” Many predicted that passing the preferential voting system would be difficult within the party leadership, where the pro-Jeong faction holds a majority. However, a settlement was reached as Jeong’s side accepted the amendment to party rules on the day, just two days before the start of candidate registration. Pro-Jeong Supreme Council members Moon Jeong-bok, Park Ji-won, and Park Gyu-hwan met with reporters after the Supreme Council meeting that day and said, “We cannot understand why they went this far,” but added, “To save the party facing a thousand-foot cliff, we will reluctantly set aside our convictions for now.” <<> The pro-Moon faction criticized Jeong for creating an appearance of reluctantly accepting preferential voting. In a Facebook post that day, Jeong wrote, “I have a lot to say, but I will refrain,” adding, “I will protect the Democratic Party, so now party members, please protect Jeong Cheong-rae.” Pro-Jeong lawmaker Kim Young-hwan also said, “I am ashamed of the name ‘democracy’ in the Democratic Party. Party members, please protect the Democratic Party.” This was an appeal to elect Jeong as party leader. A source close to Jeong stated, “Historically, those who have made concessions in rule-setting have always gained the upper hand in elections,” and “This insistence on preferential voting will ultimately backfire on the opposing camp.” Indeed, Jeong’s side expects that some party members who put Song as their first choice in preferential voting will put Jeong as their second choice instead of Kim. <<> The Democratic Party has decided to scrap the youth supreme council member system, which was introduced to attract the support of voters in their 20s and 30s. The pro-Jeong faction had opposed this as well, claiming it violated the party constitution, and their opinion was accepted. A Democratic Party official explained, “With five supreme council seats, excluding the female and youth quotas, there are effectively only three seats, and 7 to 8 candidates would have to compete. It seems the pro-Jeong side felt they would be at a disadvantage numerically.” That day, Kim Min-seok and Song Young-gil both strongly criticized the scrapping of the youth supreme council member system. <<> With about a month left until the party convention, Democratic Party leadership contenders are escalating their criticism of one another. On JTBC’s YouTube channel, Kim Min-seok commented on Jeong’s pledge not to run for president, saying, “It’s completely out of the blue. Who is interested in the presidential election right now?” On CBS Radio, Song Young-gil targeted Jeong, saying, “Just because you shout ‘Lee Jae-myung’ a few times, does that erase the ‘Myung-Jeong rivalry’? Isn’t that almost stalker-level behavior?” Furthermore, at an event for the Honam hometown association, he stated, “It’s unthinkable to fight a president who still has four years left in his term,” and even said, “In the old days, he would have been branded a traitor and decapitated to suppress the situation.” <<> In contrast, on a YouTube channel hosted by Kim Eo-jun that day, Jeong said, “To unite the traditional core support base, someone has to play a role with a single root ideology. The right person is Jeong Cheong-rae.” <<> Meanwhile, a speech by 36-year-old Kim Bo-mi, a former chair of the Gangjin County Council in South Jeolla Province, who is running in the five-way Democratic Party leadership race, has belatedly become a hot topic. During a policy presentation on the 12th, Kim directly targeted the 86-generation, which constitutes the mainstream of the Democratic Party. She said, “The democratization movement should be respected, but that shouldn’t grant them a monopoly over politics for 40 to 50 years,” and “Should a country aiming to become one of the top three AI powerhouses still have as its mainstay a generation that wielded Molotov cocktails and stones?” With Kim Min-seok, Jeong Cheong-rae, and Song Young-gil—key figures of the 86-generation—present, she was effectively calling for their retirement. Kim also said, “The Democratic Party is a ‘party of five absences’—fairness, democracy, generational change, youth, and the future have all disappeared,” and “Young people are leaving because there is neither fairness nor democracy within the party.” (선호투표는 당헌·당규 위반”이라고 해온 정청래 전 대표는 “쿨하게 받아들이겠다”고 했다. 선호투표는 과반 득표자가 없을 경우를 대비해 후보들 순위를 매겨 투표하는 것인데, 김민석 전 총리와 송영길 의원에게 유리하다는 평가가 많았다. 친명계 일각에선 “선호투표에 반발해 온 정 전 대표와 친청계가 빠르게 수용한 건 불리한 룰을 받아들이는 모습으로 당원 동정표를 얻으려는 계산”이라는 말이 나왔다.)

item.title: 11 Lawmakers from Ruling Party Propose Bill Opposing Abolition of Supplementary Investigation Rights… Party Leadership Also in Deep Thought (與의원 11명, 보완수사권 폐지 반대법 발의… 당 지도부도 고심)
item.description:
11 Lawmakers from Ruling Party Propose Bill Opposing Abolition of Supplementary Investigation Rights… Party Leadership Also in Deep Thought (與의원 11명, 보완수사권 폐지 반대법 발의… 당 지도부도 고심)

On the 14th, 11 lawmakers from the Democratic Party of Korea proposed a revision to the Criminal Procedure Act that partially retains the prosecution's supplementary investigation rights. This comes as the party leadership pushes for the complete abolition of supplementary investigation rights before the August 17 national convention. The incident involving Jang Yoon-gi in Gwangju, South Jeolla, where the prosecution's supplementary investigation revealed attempts by the police to cover up or downplay a crime, served as a catalyst. Although the Democratic Party stated on the same day that "abolishing supplementary investigation rights is the principle," some voices argued that "with differing opinions within the party, a conclusion should be reached after further deliberation." <<> Democratic Party lawmaker Hong Ki-won led the proposal of the amendment opposing the complete abolition of supplementary investigation rights. The list of proposers includes primarily legal professionals: former prosecutors Joo Cheol-hyun and Park Gyun-taek, former judge Park Hee-seung, and lawyers Min Hong-chul, Lee So-young, Kwak Sang-eon, and Kim Nam-hee. Also joining as proposers were pro-Moon lawmaker Ko Min-jung, who is running in the August 17 party leadership election, and pro-Lee lawmakers Moon Jin-seok and Mo Kyung-jong. Lawmaker Hong stated, "While we share the same intent, some lawmakers could not participate in the joint proposal because they hold party positions or it could affect the national convention," and added, "There were also lawmakers who agreed with the basic direction (of partially retaining supplementary investigation rights) but did not participate because they disagreed with some details." The National Assembly's Legislation and Judiciary Committee plans to discuss this bill along with the amendment previously proposed by the party's task force in the subcommittee on bill review. <<> The amendment led by Lawmaker Hong allows prosecutors to conduct supplementary investigations for crimes targeting the socially vulnerable and everyday crimes. It also includes a provision requiring all cases involving sexual violence, elder abuse, and similar crimes to be forwarded for investigation. Lawmaker Hong said, "Currently, each frontline police investigator handles about 50 cases," and argued that "if supplementary investigation rights are completely abolished, all cases would have to proceed through requests for supplementary investigation, leading to significant delays and inevitably more inadequate investigations." <<> Although some Democratic Party lawmakers had previously expressed concerns about abolishing supplementary investigation rights, they refrained from public statements due to concerns about attacks from hardline supporters within the ruling bloc. However, following the bill's proposal, it was reported that over 10 lawmakers expressed concerns about the complete abolition of supplementary investigation rights during a general meeting of lawmakers, and no conclusion was reached. This suggests a shift in the Democratic Party's discussion on revising the Criminal Procedure Act, which had overwhelmingly leaned toward the complete abolition of the prosecution's supplementary investigation rights. <<> Acting Party Leader Han Byung-do stated in his opening remarks at the general meeting, "We must complete the final puzzle of prosecutorial reform through a revision of the Criminal Procedure Act centered on the complete abolition of supplementary investigation rights," while acknowledging that "I am well aware that some concerns have been raised." Notably, when asked by some lawmakers whether "the decision to abolish supplementary investigation rights was set as party policy at the February general meeting," he reportedly replied, "It was not party policy." This implies that while opinions were gathered, the formal ratification process was not completed, so it does not constitute official party policy. <<> With opposition to the complete abolition of supplementary investigation rights emerging within the party, the leadership, which had called for "handling the bill in a plenary session of the National Assembly before the August national convention," has fallen into deep thought. A key leadership lawmaker said, "Initially, President Lee Jae-myung was in favor of allowing exceptions to the abolition of supplementary investigation rights, but under pressure from hardliners, he temporarily delegated full authority on this matter to the party," and added, "The amendment proposed by Lawmaker Hong and others is, in fact, very similar to the initial draft of the government's bill, which reflected the president's thinking." President Lee remarked at a cabinet meeting, "When you stick the needle in sharply, the syringe breaks if the person tenses up out of fear. You have to go gently. Reform is similar," and a ruling bloc official interpreted this as "a remark aimed at the hardliners pushing for the abolition of supplementary investigation rights." <<> However, hardliners within the Democratic Party reiterated their demand for the complete abolition of supplementary investigation rights on the same day. Former Party Leader Jung Cheong-rae, who is running in the party leadership election, wrote on Facebook that "the complete abolition of supplementary investigation rights is the flag and symbol of the Democratic Party's prosecutorial reform." Lawmaker Kim Yong-min held a press conference and stated, "Even partially retaining supplementary investigation rights is opening the door to returning to the starting point of prosecutorial reform." <<> Hardline supporters of the ruling bloc reacted by urging Democratic Party lawmakers who opposed the abolition of supplementary investigation rights to "resign from their positions." In pro-government communities like YouTuber Kim Eo-joon's "Ddanji Ilbo," posts naming specific lawmakers and insisting they "must be eliminated from candidate nominations" lined up. Comments such as "Were you lobbied by the prosecution?" and "Watermelon (green on the outside, red on the inside; referring to lawmakers who are ostensibly Democratic Party but sympathetic to the People Power Party), just wait and see" were posted on the lawmakers' social media accounts. There were also claims that lawmakers Kim Nam-hee and Park Gyun-taek, who are members of the Legislation and Judiciary Committee and known to oppose the complete abolition of supplementary investigation rights, should be moved to other standing committees. (더불어민주당 의원 11명이 14일 검찰의 보완수사권을 일부 존치하는 내용의 형사소송법 개정안을 발의했다. 당 지도부가 8·17 전당대회 전 보완수사권 완전 폐지를 추진하고 있는 가운데 반대 목소리를 낸 것이다. 검찰 보완수사로 경찰의 범죄 은폐·축소 정황이 드러난 전남광주 장윤기 사건이 계기가 됐다. 민주당은 이날도 “보완수사권 폐지가 원칙”이라고 밝혔지만, 일각에선 “당내 이견이 있는 만큼 더 숙의한 뒤 결론을 내려야 한다”는 주장이 나왔다.)

item.title: "Let's recount" says special committee chair from PPP… PPP committee members say "Special counsel first" (국힘 소속 특위 위원장 “재검표를”… 국힘 특위 위원들은 “특검이 먼저”)
item.description:
"Let's recount" says special committee chair from PPP… PPP committee members say "Special counsel first" (국힘 소속 특위 위원장 “재검표를”… 국힘 특위 위원들은 “특검이 먼저”)

The National Assembly's special committee investigating the ballot shortage incident attempted on the 14th to propose a motion for recounting ballots stored at the handball stadium in Olympic Park, Songpa-gu, Seoul, but the move fell through due to opposition from some People Power Party (PPP) lawmakers. They argue, "A special counsel must be launched first, so we cannot allow the election commission to touch the ballots beforehand." The handball stadium was used as a vote-counting site for Songpa-gu during the June 3 local elections, but 2.47 million ballots whose counting had been completed are stored there after citizens protesting the ballot shortage gathered at the venue. <<> Yoon Sang-hyun, the chair of the special committee and a member of the PPP, stated at a hearing held that morning, "To resolve the public's doubts, we must now reach a conclusion on discussing a public recount of the ballots." Chair Yoon had proposed a recount on the 5th. <<> Yoon Gun-young, the Democratic Party's secretary on the special committee, said, "The Democratic Party's official stance is an immediate recount." The National Election Commission (NEC) has indicated that if the ruling and opposition parties reach an agreement, it can conduct a recount of both the ballots stored at the handball stadium and the so-called 'twin vote' phenomenon, where early voting results for candidates in the local elections were identical. <<> In contrast, PPP lawmakers on the special committee opposed an immediate recount. Rep. Joo Jin-woo said, "If a special counsel is established, the ballot boxes will become subject to seizure and search—so having the NEC directly deploy its staff for a recount beforehand is problematic." This implies a risk of evidence tampering. Rep. Shin Dong-wook added, "I hear the Democratic Party is showing no sincerity in the special counsel negotiations. I find it hard to understand why they're suddenly pushing for a recount as a party stance. The recount will very likely end up as just a show by the special committee." The PPP views the Democratic Party's real intention as wanting to quickly disperse the citizens gathered in front of Olympic Park. <<> As the PPP lawmakers' opposition prevented the motion from being proposed that day, the Democratic Party pushed back. Rep. Jeon Yong-gi said, "The only way to resolve the Jamsil situation is to prove there was no election fraud. I wish the PPP would be more honest. I think the PPP is enjoying this situation." He added, "If they try to gain political advantage by exploiting social chaos, that ultimately ties them to insurrectionist forces." In response, PPP Rep. Shin said, "Are you saying the citizens out at Olympic Park are enjoying this? Did the Democratic Party enjoy it when the Sewol ferry disaster and the Itaewon tragedy happened?" <<> A ruling party source commented, "It's an absurd situation where the chair, who is from the PPP, first proposed the recount, but the PPP is opposing it." <<> At the hearing that day, allegations also emerged of a so-called "Seonpia (NEC mafia) cartel," where the NEC allegedly funneled contracts to a former employee's family company. Rep. Joo claimed that the total value of contracts signed between the NEC and companies involving former NEC executives and their families reached 17.5 billion won. He asked, "It's not like they're handing out special bonuses; is it appropriate to award so many non-competitive contracts like that?" Acting NEC Chair Wi Cheol-hwan responded, "It is inappropriate." (투표용지 부족 사태를 조사 중인 국회 국정조사 특별위원회가 14일 서울 송파구 올림픽공원 핸드볼경기장 내 보관 중인 투표지를 재검표하는 안건을 상정하려 했지만 일부 국민의힘 의원의 반대로 무산됐다. 이들은 “특검을 해야 하기 때문에 그전에 선관위가 투표지에 손을 대게 해선 안 된다”는 입장이다. 핸드볼경기장은 6·3 지방선거 당시 송파구 개표소로 쓰였지만 투표용지 부족 사태에 항의하는 시민들이 집결하면서 개표가 끝난 투표지 247만장이 경기장 내에 보관 중이다.)

item.title: Oh Se-hoon: "Seoul's housing administration is…" President Lee: "Let's talk about that later." (오세훈 “서울 주택 행정은…” 李대통령 “그 얘기는 나중에 하시죠”)
item.description:
Oh Se-hoon: "Seoul's housing administration is…" President Lee: "Let's talk about that later." (오세훈 “서울 주택 행정은…” 李대통령 “그 얘기는 나중에 하시죠”)

President Lee Jae-myung stated at the Cabinet meeting on the 14th regarding real estate taxation, "The problem is that with all these deductions and exemptions, the system has been twisted so much that it fails to fulfill its basic function." The government plans to hold a major real estate forum on the 23rd, chaired by President Lee, to discuss matters such as property taxes, differential taxation between single-homeowner residents and non-residents or multiple-homeowners, and the price threshold for ultra-high-value homes, and will announce the direction of tax reform. At that day's Cabinet meeting, Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon, a member of the People Power Party, attended intending to propose real estate policies but was unable to speak. <<> The government tabled the "Plan for Collecting Public Opinions on Real Estate Policy" as an agenda item for the Cabinet meeting. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance Koo Yoon-cheol reported on contentious issues in real estate tax reform, noting that raising property taxes could harm elderly actual homeowners. President Lee responded, "I felt a hint of personal sentiment from the Deputy Prime Minister regarding his own retirement planning." <<> That day's Cabinet meeting was also broadcast live on YouTube. President Lee said, "If citizens think it would be good to impose a differentiated (higher) burden on ultra-high-value homes, please press 1; if you disagree, please press 2." When Director of the Office for Government Policy Coordination Im Ki-keun reported, "Number 1 has a lot of responses in the comments," President Lee remarked, "So there's general agreement on strengthening the burden on ultra-high-value homes, even for a single home occupied by the owner." <<> President Lee also suggested surveying the classification threshold for ultra-high-value homes, saying, "Please press 1 for homes worth 1 billion won or more, 2 for 2 billion or more, 3 for 3 billion or more, etc." Upon hearing that many comments cited 2 (2 billion won) or 3 (3 billion won), President Lee said, "That's unexpected; I thought it would be around 5 billion won." According to real estate data firm Real Estate R114, the average market price of an apartment in Seoul as of the 10th was 1.67969 billion won. After viewing the comments, President Lee stated, "Tax equity is crucial, but in the housing sector, the tax system has been significantly distorted or warped." He added, "There's controversy over whether it's fair to grant the same exemption for a single ultra-high-value home worth 10 billion won, just because it's owner-occupied." <<> At that moment, Mayor Oh, observing from the back row, requested to speak, asking, "May I say something?" Prime Minister Han Sung-sook replied, "We'll receive the mayor's suggestions in writing." Prior to the Cabinet meeting, the Seoul Metropolitan Government had submitted a 30-page document titled "Real Estate Market Issue Analysis and Government Policy Recommendations" to the government, covering deregulation of redevelopment projects, revitalization of private rental housing, and tax reform measures. <<> President Lee said, "There's a general perception inside and outside the market that Seoul's housing supply is very insufficient; please add a report on the specific causes and current status of why supply is delayed and not working." Mayor Oh responded, "It's already in the report." During the last local elections, when real estate became an issue, the Democratic Party attacked Mayor Oh for a decline in the supply of apartments and villas in Seoul during his tenure. Mayor Oh attributed this to former Seoul Mayor Park Won-soon, a Democrat, having canceled numerous redevelopment zones, and had said, "If elected as Seoul Mayor, I'll attend Cabinet meetings to convey public sentiment on real estate to President Lee." <<> As the meeting ended, President Lee sought out Mayor Oh and said, "Please give a very brief greeting." When Mayor Oh began, "At the Cabinet meeting, I really wanted to talk about Seoul's housing administration…" President Lee interrupted, "Let's talk about that later." After the Cabinet meeting, Mayor Oh held a press conference at Seoul City Hall and said, "I had prepared a short but well-organized statement, but it's deeply regrettable that I didn't get the chance to deliver it." <<> Meanwhile, during the meeting, President Lee mentioned that his home in Bundang-gu, Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, had been sold, saying, "I no longer have a house." President Lee had listed his apartment (exclusive area 164㎡) at Yangji Village Kumho 1 Complex in Bundang for sale in February. He purchased it in 1998 for 360 million won, and recent asking prices were around 3 to 3.1 billion won. It is reported that President Lee listed the apartment at 2.9 billion won, below market value, and it sold at that price. In political circles, this was interpreted as an attempt to emphasize his detachment from the issue before pushing forward with real estate tax reform. (이재명 대통령이 14일 국무회의에서 부동산 세제에 대해 “이렇게 공제해 주고, 저렇게 빼주고, 너무 많이 변형을 해서 조세의 기본적 기능을 못 하고 있는 게 문제”라고 했다. 정부는 오는 23일 이 대통령 주재로 부동산 대토론회를 열어 보유세, 실거주 1주택과 비거주·다주택 차등 과세, 초고가 주택 가격 기준 등을 논의하고 세제 개편 방향을 발표할 예정이다. 이날 국무회의에는 국민의힘 소속인 오세훈 서울시장이 배석해 부동산 정책을 제안하려 했지만 발언 기회를 얻지 못했다.)

]]>

item.title: Government Holds Emergency Meeting Over Renewed US-Iran Conflict… S. Korean Prime Minister: “Supply Chain Instability Is Now a Constant” (미국-이란 충돌 재발에 정부 비상 회의… 韓총리 “이제 공급망 불안은 상수”)
item.description:
Government Holds Emergency Meeting Over Renewed US-Iran Conflict… S. Korean Prime Minister: “Supply Chain Instability Is Now a Constant” (미국-이란 충돌 재발에 정부 비상 회의… 韓총리 “이제 공급망 불안은 상수”)

As the US-Iran ceasefire agreement collapsed and the US resumed airstrikes against Iran, the South Korean government held an emergency meeting on the 15th to assess the economic situation and its response readiness. Prime Minister Han Seong-suk emphasized, "We must treat international oil price and supply chain instability as a constant and push forward our short- and long-term measures." (미국과 이란의 휴전 합의가 깨지고 미국이 대이란 공습을 재개하자 정부가 15일 비상 회의를 열어 경제 상황과 정부 대응 태세를 점검했다. 한성숙 국무총리는 “국제 유가 공급망 불안을 상수로 보고, 우리의 장단기 대책을 추진해 나가야 한다”고 강조했다.)

The government convened the emergency economic review meeting at the Seoul Government Complex that morning, chaired by Prime Minister Han. This came just 15 days after an emergency economic review meeting chaired by President Lee Jae-myung on the 30th of last month wrapped up an assessment of emergency responses related to the Middle East war. Attending the meeting were senior officials from the Ministry of Economy and Finance, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Ministry of SMEs and Startups, Financial Services Commission, Office for Government Policy Coordination, and the Prime Minister's Secretariat. (정부는 이날 아침 정부서울청사에서 한 총리 주재로 비상 경제 점검 회의를 열었다. 지난달 30일 이재명 대통령 주재로 비상 경제 점검 회의를 열어 중동 전쟁 관련 비상 대응 점검을 마무리한 지 15일 만이다. 이날 회의에는 재정경제부, 외교부, 문화체육관광부, 농림축산식품부, 산업통상부, 해양수산부, 중소벤처기업부, 금융위원회, 국무조정실, 국무총리비서실 고위 관계자들이 참석했다.)

Prime Minister Han stated, "Recently, armed clashes between the US and Iran have been recurring, and the negotiations to end the war are at risk of collapsing," adding, "International oil prices, which had been stabilizing, are rising again, and this is directly exerting pressure on our prices and supply chains." (한 총리는 “최근 미국·이란 간 무력 충돌이 다시 반복되고 있고, 종전 협상도 자칫 좌초 위기에 놓여 있는 상황”이라며 “안정화되던 국제 유가도 다시 상승하고 있고, 이는 고스란히 우리 물가와 공급망에 압박을 가하고 있다”고 했다.)

He continued, "We must once again sharpen the government's response posture," and stressed, "We must treat international oil price and supply chain instability as a constant and push forward our short-term and long-term measures." (이어 “정부의 대응 태세를 다시 한번 가다듬어야 한다”며 “국제유가 공급망 불안을 상수로 보고, 우리의 장·단기 대책을 추진해 나가야 한다”고 했다.)

He further instructed, "Please thoroughly review the current supply and demand situation for crude oil and naphtha, and actively promote the use of alternative routes and diversification of supply chains." He also added, "Closely monitor the situation to ensure that the government's response to changes in circumstances is carried out swiftly." (그러면서 “현재의 원유, 나프타 등 수급 상황을 철저히 점검하고, 우회 경로 이용과 공급망 다변화를 적극 추진해 주시기를 바란다”고 주문했다. “상황 변화에 따른 정부의 대응도 신속하게 이뤄질 수 있도록 상황도 면밀히 모니터링해 달라”고도 했다.)

Prime Minister Han also noted, "This is a time when the lives of ordinary people and vulnerable groups are becoming more difficult due to a combination of energy price hikes and seasonal disaster factors such as the onset of intense heat and heavy rain," and urged, "Related ministries should do their utmost to prevent the energy shock originating from the Middle East from spilling over into people's livelihoods, and also look into the hardships faced by producers such as farmers and fishers." (한 총리는 또 “에너지 가격 상승에 본격적인 무더위와 폭우 등 계절적 재난 요인까지 겹치면서 서민과 취약 계층 삶이 어려워지는 시기”라며 “관계 부처는 중동발 에너지 충격이 민생에 전이되지 않도록 만전을 기해 주고, 농어민 등 생산자의 어려움을 살펴 달라”고 했다.)

Meanwhile, referring to the 'Second Half Economic Growth Strategy' announced by the government the previous day, Prime Minister Han said, "This strategy is the government's commitment to overcoming the Middle East crisis, improving the economic system, and boosting the potential growth rate." He added, "Through bold regulatory innovation and investment in cutting-edge future industries, we must complete the first year of a great economic leap that is unshaken by external shocks." He advised each ministry, "Please carry out the tasks we have promised to the people with a sense of mission so that they can be implemented swiftly." (한 총리는 한편 전날 정부가 발표한 ‘하반기 경제 성장 전략’을 거론하면서 “이번 전략은 중동 위기 극복을 넘어 경제 체제를 개선하고 잠재 성장률을 반등시키기 위한 정부의 약속”이라고 했다. 그러면서 “과감한 규제 혁신과 첨단 미래 산업에 대한 투자를 통해, 대외 충격에 흔들리지 않는 경제 대도약의 원년을 완성해야 한다”고 했다. 각 부처에는 “국민께 약속드린 과제들이 신속하게 집행될 수 있도록 사명감을 갖고 챙겨 달라”고 했다.)

item.title: President Lee: "Reporting Corruption as a Profession Isn't a Bad Thing... Professional Whistleblowers Shouldn't Be Penalized" (李대통령 “부정부패 신고, 업으로 하는 것도 나쁘지 않아...전문 신고꾼에 불이익 안돼”)
item.description:
President Lee Jae-myung stated on the 15th, "I don't see anything wrong with uncovering and reporting corruption, or even making a profession out of it," adding, "What's wrong with that?" (이재명 대통령은 15일 “부정부패를 발굴해 신고하거나 업으로 하는 것을 나쁘다고 보지 않는다”며 “그게 왜 나쁜가”라고 했다.)

During a briefing from the Ministry of Economy and Finance and other agencies at the Blue House that day, President Lee remarked, "I believe that reporting and rooting out corruption contributes much more to the nation or the community." He noted that there seem to be cases where professional whistleblowers are not properly receiving their rewards, saying, "It would be better to ensure they aren't penalized simply for being professional whistleblowers." (이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 열린 재정경제부 등의 업무 보고에서 “신고해서 발본색원하는 것이 훨씬 더 국가 또는 공동체에 기여하는 것이라 생각한다”며 이같이 말했다. 이 대통령은 신고를 전문으로 하는 사람에게 포상금이 제대로 지급되지 않는 사례도 있는 것 같다면서 “전문 신고꾼이다, 이런 이유로 불이익 주지 않게 하는 게 좋을 것 같다”고 했다.)

This comment from President Lee came amid his emphasis on the need to strengthen the 'subsidy management system.' He argued that while rewards are given for reporting the misuse of subsidies, there is no reason to penalize those who engage in such activities with the aim of earning these rewards. (이 대통령의 이런 언급은 ‘보조금 관리 시스템’의 강화 필요성을 강조하는 과정에서 나왔다. 보조금의 부정 집행을 신고할 경우 포상금을 지급하는데, 이런 종류의 포상금을 목표로 활동하는 사람들을 제재할 이유가 없다는 것이다.)

President Lee said, "The government's policy is that when a crime is reported and the state recovers the funds, roughly 30% of the recovered amount is typically paid to the reporter or contributor. There's no need to prohibit someone from forming a company to professionally report such cases and make money." (이 대통령은 “범죄행위를 신고해 국가가 환수하면 그 금액의 30% 정도는 기본적으로 신고자 또는 기여자에게 지급한다는 게 정부의 방침”이라며 “이걸 회사를 만들어서 전문적으로 신고하고 돈 벌겠다고 하는 것을 금지할 필요가 없다”고 했다.)

President Lee also stressed the need for stronger penalties against improper benefit claims, stating, "We are too lenient. If it's a mistake, it can be corrected, but if someone deliberately engages in fraudulent claims, that company should be barred from further opportunities or even dissolved. The reality is that the penalties are weak." (이 대통령은 부정수급에 대한 제재도 강하게 이뤄져야 한다면서 “너무 온정적이다”라며 “실수면 시정하면 되지만 일부러 부정 수급을 위해 한다고 한다면 그 회사는 아예 (기회를) 안 주거나 해산시키든지 해야 하는데 제재가 약한 것이 사실”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Jang Dong-hyuk to Han Dong-hoon: "Driving People Power Party into a Dead End and Then Seeking Reinstatement?...Loss of Justification" (장동혁, 한동훈에 “국민의힘 사지로 몰고 복당?...명분 상실”)
item.description:
People Power Party leader Jang Dong-hyuk commented on the speculation about independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon's reinstatement, saying, "He wants to remain as someone who prevented martial law and led the impeachment, while driving Daegu Mayor Choo Kyung-ho into a corner and pushing the People Power Party almost to the edge of a cliff—what kind of logic is it to suddenly seek reinstatement into the People Power Party?" (국민의힘 장동혁 대표가 무소속 한동훈 의원 복당설에 대해 “자신은 계엄을 막고 탄핵을 주도한 사람으로 남고, 추경호 대구시장을 사지로 몰고, 국민의힘을 거의 낭떠러지로 몰아넣고 갑자기 국민의힘에 복당하겠다는 게 도대체 무슨 논리냐”고 했다.)

Jang made these remarks while appearing on the YouTube channel Pen & Mike TV this morning, referencing the trial of Daegu Mayor Choo Kyung-ho, who was the People Power Party's floor leader during the December 3, 2024, emergency martial law incident and is now being charged with obstructing a vote to lift martial law. (장 대표는 이날 오전 유튜브 펜앤마이크TV에 출연해 2024년 12월 3일 비상계엄 사태 당시 국민의힘 원내대표였던 추경호 대구시장의 비상계엄 해제 표결 방해 혐의 재판을 언급하며 이같이 밝혔다.)

He brought up the recent exchange between lawmaker Ahn Cheol-soo and Han Dong-hoon, noting that Ahn testified in Choo’s trial, stating, "To my knowledge, it was then-party leader Han Dong-hoon who first notified People Power Party lawmakers to gather at the party headquarters rather than the National Assembly." Jang then questioned, "If Han keeps insisting that Ahn's testimony is wrong, does that mean Choo should be punished as an accomplice to insurrection?" (그는 최근 안철수 의원이 추 시장 재판에 출석해 “국민의힘 의원들에게 국회가 아닌 당사로 모이라고 처음 공지한 인물이 한동훈 당시 당 대표로 안다”고 언급했고, 이를 두고 한 의원과 설전을 벌인 것을 거론하며 “(한 의원은) 안 의원이 증언한 것에 대해 계속 틀렸다고 주장하면, 추 시장은 내란죄 공범으로 처벌을 받으란 것이냐”고 했다.)

He continued, "If Han had simply said, 'Yes, I was the one who first suggested going to the party headquarters,' this case would have taken an entirely different turn. Now, the justification for discussing Han's reinstatement has been lost. No foundation for it remains whatsoever." (그러면서 “한 의원이 ‘당사로 가자고 먼저 얘기한 건 접니다’라고만 했으면 이 사건은 전혀 다른 국면으로 갔을 것”이라며 “이제 한 의원의 복당에 대해 언급할 만한 명분이 상실됐다. 그 어떤 기반도 이제는 남아 있지 않다”고 했다.)

Regarding criticism that the "subtraction politics" emerged after Han's expulsion, Jang said, "What if you bring in a sniper who is an excellent shot, but then he turns his incredible marksmanship against your own side? Isn't that a disaster?" (장 대표는 한 의원 제명 이후 ‘뺄셈 정치’라는 비판이 나오는 데 대해서도 “정말 총을 잘 쏘는 스나이퍼를 우리 편으로 데려왔는데, 그 사람이 기가 막힌 총솜씨를 우리 편을 향해서 쓴다는 건 재앙 아니겠느냐”고 했다.)

He added, "The issue of Han's expulsion goes beyond party-disrupting acts into criminal acts. It is simply inappropriate to even discuss reinstating someone who was expelled for criminal behavior." (그러면서 “한 의원의 제명 문제는 해당 행위를 넘어서서 범죄 행위”라며 “범죄 행위로 제명당한 사람에 대해서 복당을 거론하는 것 자체가 적절하지 않다”고 했다.)
